retrieved_articles.title: Causes and Effects of Climate Change | United Nations
retrieved_articles.body: [Climate Action](/en/climatechange) # Causes and Effects of Climate Change Fossil fuels – coal, oil and gas – are by far the largest contributor to global climate change, accounting for around 68 per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions and nearly 90 per cent of all carbon dioxide emissions. As greenhouse gas emissions blanket the Earth, they trap the sun’s heat. Because of this, the planet is warming up and the climate is changing. The world is now warming faster than at any point in recorded history. Warmer temperatures over time are changing weather patterns and disrupting the usual balance of nature. This poses many risks to human beings and all other forms of life on Earth. ## [Causes of Climate Change](#collapseOne) **Generating power** A large chunk of global emissions comes from burning fossil fuels to produce electricity and heat. Most electricity is still generated by burning coal, oil, or gas, which produces carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide – powerful greenhouse gases that blanket the Earth and trap the sun’s heat.
